title: Authorities Find CJNG Clandestine 'Hospital' in Tecalitlán, Jalisco — 8 Rescued, 6 Detained
detail: On September 10, 2026, a joint operation by the Jalisco Prosecutor's Office (Fiscalía del Estado), the National Guard, and SEDENA raided a property in Tecalitlán, southern Jalisco, that investigators say CJNG used as a clandestine recovery clinic for wounded members. The property was located after investigators traced the July 21 disappearance of a 20-year-old man from Tlaquepaque to Tecalitlán. Eight men, ages 16 to 43 and from Mexico City, Guerrero, Michoacán, Sinaloa, and Jalisco, were found held against their will at the site — some had undergone surgery and two were using crutches. Authorities detained five men and one woman, ages 21-48 and from Jalisco, Colima, Nayarit, and Michoacán, on charges of human trafficking and forced disappearance. Seized items included medications, orthopedic boots and crutches, marijuana, tactical clothing, and roughly a hundred rounds of high-caliber ammunition. On September 11, federal Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch confirmed federal authorities (FGR) were investigating the site alongside Jalisco state authorities, describing it as a facility CJNG used to treat members 'heridos de la propia delincuencia organizada' (wounded in the group's own criminal activity). The Jalisco Prosecutor's Office noted similarities to the 2025 Rancho Izaguirre case; the investigation continues into possible involvement of local medical personnel.

media.caption: Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch confirms federal investigation of the Tecalitlán, Jalisco clandestine hospital linked to CJNG

confidenceReason: The raid, victims, detainees, and seized items are confirmed by the Jalisco Prosecutor's Office and corroborated by the federal Security Secretary's Sep 11 statement and two independent Tier-2 outlets; the facility's precise CJNG operational role remains under investigation.

title: Edomex Prosecutors Arrest Alleged 'Los Vallarta' Financial Operator, CJNG-Linked Cell, Over La Paz Bar Killing
detail: The State of Mexico Attorney General's Office (FGJEM) executed an arrest warrant against José Eduardo 'N,' identified as a probable financial operator of 'Los Vallarta,' a criminal cell prosecutors describe as linked to CJNG operating in municipalities in the eastern State of Mexico. He is accused of participating in the August 1, 2026 killing of a man at the 'La Malquerida D'Oro' bar in La Paz municipality — five suspects arrived by motorcycle and car, and one entered the bar and shot the victim before the group fled. The FGJEM attributes homicides, drug sales and distribution, extortion, and kidnappings in eastern Edomex municipalities to 'Los Vallarta.' The detainee was transferred to a state penitentiary in eastern Mexico State; he faces a potential sentence of up to 70 years if convicted.

media.caption: State of Mexico authorities detain an alleged 'Los Vallarta' financial operator tied to CJNG in the La Paz bar killing case

confidenceReason: The arrest, charges, and cell description are confirmed by the State of Mexico Attorney General's Office and corroborated by two independent Tier-2 outlets; the cell's precise organizational ties to CJNG rest on the FGJEM's characterization.
